highlights.title: Uncanny and unappetizing: appetites spoil as AI images take over food menus
highlights.summary: Consumers are increasingly encountering AI-generated images on food menus such as leathery meat and bread resembling reptile skin. During a recent lunch break, Jill Sennett saw something so unappetizing she had to share it with her 26,000 X followers: Artificial intelligence-generated menu images…
body: The images were reshared by more than 500 people who similarly expressed their disgust. Eating is “such an essential human experience”, said Sennett, a 37-year-old nurse in Denver. “I think it’s a bad cultural thing that restaurants are converting to these horrific, uncanny food images that are unappetizing.”
Still, Sennett ordered chicken and macaroni and cheese. It was one of her only lunch options, and she had eaten there before.

Increasingly, consumers are encountering AI-generated images of food on restaurant menus or marketing material. Diners like Sennett say the images are unappealing and misleading, while restaurants say they’re trying to cut costs at a time when food and labor prices are high, so profit margins are slim.
A 2026 report from the National Restaurant Association found 26% of restaurant operators use AI to help with marketing, inventory management, employee scheduling, optimizing menus and taking orders.

highlights.title: Seattle Times and Newsday are the latest publications to sue OpenAI and Microsoft
highlights.summary: Two more news organizations are suing OpenAI and Microsoft over the supposed use of their journalism to train AI.
body: A lawsuit filed by The Seattle Times and Newsday argued that with the advent of AI, the journalism industry could become “broken beyond repair.” The lawsuit described generative AI as “a snake eating its own tail” that could “destroy the very organizations” that produce the content it’s trained on.

“AI products like ChatGPT and CoPilot are touted as producers of content, but in fact they are rapacious consumers, devouring human-authored content and delivering back to the world copies and derivative imitations of that same original content they consumed to achieve their commercial objectives,” the lawsuit said.

Back in 2023, The New York Times sued OpenAI and its partner/investor Microsoft over alleged copyright infringement; other publications have followed suit as the case continued. The Seattle Times’ lawsuit is particularly notable because Microsoft and OpenAI have funded some of the organization’s journalism projects and fellowships.
A Microsoft spokesperson told GeekWire that the company is “surprised by the lawsuit” but is “always happy to sit down and explore solutions to this type of dispute.”

highlights.title: 7 Huge Differences Between Christopher Nolan's 'Interstellar' and Steven Spielberg's Original Script
highlights.summary: But before Christopher Nolan signed on as the director of Interstellar, the director was none other than Steven Spielberg, who developed the story with Nolan’s screenwriter brother, Jonathan Nolan.
body: More than six weeks after its premiere, Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey is still going strong at the box office. Recently, it surpassed Deadpool & Wolverine to become the highest-grossing R-rated film of all time. As such, the celebration of Nolan’s entire filmography continues, including his 2014 sci-fi epic, Interstellar, which is about a team of astronauts traveling into deep space to find a new home for humans before the Earth becomes uninhabitable.

The script of Spielberg’s version of the film is accessible online, though. If you read it, it's clear that we would have gotten a much different movie. Here are the seven biggest differences between the Interstellar we got from Christopher Nolan and the version we almost got from Steven Spielberg.

In Christopher Nolan’s version of Interstellar, Matthew McConaughey’s character Cooper was a trained NASA pilot before the events of the film, but NASA had shut down before he could go on any missions. In Spielberg’s version, Cooper is merely a crafty engineer who stumbles upon a space probe returning from deep space. The probe leads him to the secret NASA base where he is then selected for the space mission that’s about to leave Earth.

highlights.title: I slept on a 550lb mattress made of just cotton, wool and coils for a month. Here's the case for old-school beds
highlights.summary: This eco-friendly mattress made from organic materials as a nice balance of give and underlying firmness, though it’s pretty bouncy. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: Sleep sits at the base of psychologist Abraham Maslow’s famous pyramid of needs, and it’s especially frustrating when a good night’s rest evades your grasp. Personally, thanks to a combination of a bad back and a sleep disorder, it’s all about the right mattress.

For nearly a month, I tested the Naturepedic Serenade, the cheapest mattress from an eco-friendly brand that offers three firmness options: Plush, Cushion-Firm and Firm, all made from cotton and organic materials rather than chemical foams. I tried a queen-sized firm version – I favor a mattress that supports me while sleeping on my back or side. And after a few weeks’ rest, I’m pleased to report that it is a great combination: I got a comfortable night’s sleep with reassuringly firm support and a little bit of give.

I slept on the mattress with my wife, my dog and our two cats for several weeks, keeping notes on how well we (the humans) slept, and using my Apple Watch to track my sleep patterns. We invited others to lay down and test the comfort of the mattress, and I also used weights to simulate different body types using the mattress.
The give: how much you sink into the mattress when you lie on it.
points: This eco-friendly mattress made from organic materials as a nice balance of give and underlying firmness, though it’s pretty bouncy.

If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

The 6 Plus is a light update to last year’s Fairphone 6, which my colleague Dominic Preston reviewed and found very easy to recommend. The 6 Plus builds on it with a newer midrange Snapdragon chipset and a new color treatment. Fairphone says it’s cobalt; we know it around these parts as blurple. Otherwise, the phone is basically the same, and the replacement parts sold by Fairphone work interchangeably with both models. But above all, this phone is just fine. highlights.title: Hikers rescued after using Google Gemini for planning
highlights.summary: The sheriff’s office said the hikers “were advised by Gemini to bring far less food and water than their group required."
body: Three hikers were rescued from California’s Mount Shasta this week after using Google’s AI chatbot Gemini to plan their expedition, according to the Chicago Tribune.

A report from the Siskiyou County sheriff’s office said that three young men set off on their hike at 3am and — although hikers are told to turn around if they haven’t reached the summit by noon — they made it to the top at 7pm.

The trio then tried to descend in the dark, called the sheriff’s office to ask for directions, and spent the night in Mud Creek Canyon before being rescued the next morning by Forest Service rangers and volunteers.

“It is always advisable to call the local USFS Mount Shasta ranger station ahead of your trip to ensure you have the most accurate information, and to never rely solely on AI for your trip planning,” the sheriff’s office said.

highlights.title: 55 Years Later, Stanley Kubrick's Gritty Sci-Fi Masterpiece Is Officially Back on Streaming
highlights.summary: Stanley Kubrick marks a before-and-after in the history of cinema. Few directors have received as much acclaim in life and death, admired by peers and audiences alike.
body: One of his boldest and most uncomfortable movies in a career known for pushing audiences to their limits was A Clockwork Orange. It’s now available on HBO Max.

Based on Anthony Burgess’ novel of the same name, A Clockwork Orange is set in a dystopian near-future Britain, trailing Alex DeLarge (Malcolm McDowell), a terrible young man. As a charming hoodlum speaking in a slang created by Burgess, Alex is instantly memorable, parading through the streets of London with his “droogs” while on the hunt for robbery and rape. Together, they bond as they get drunk, beat up homeless people, and break into strangers’ homes. By day, Alex sleeps in his parents' apartment, skipping school and finding girls to sleep with while the house is empty — rinse and repeat. He’s fully satisfied with his life, feeling no remorse or showing the inklings of a conscience.

highlights.title: Competitive Pokémon is on phones now, but you still need a Switch to become a champion
highlights.summary: To get started with competitive Pokémon battles, all you need is your phone. But to compete at the highest level, like at the Pokémon World Championships, you're going to need a Switch. And there doesn't seem to be a good reason why.
body: The mobile version of Pokémon Champions isn’t allowed at high-level tournaments, but it’s unclear why.

Battle simulator Pokémon Champions originally launched on the Switch and Switch 2 in April, with the mobile version following in June. The experience is nearly identical across the game’s versions; since it’s cross-platform, the choice really comes down to what devices you own and whether you prefer tapping or using a controller. I find myself playing Champions on my phone more often just because it’s always in my pocket and I’m blessed with unlimited data.

But at this year’s World Championships, the mobile version of Champions wasn’t allowed in competition. As of September 1st, certain local tournaments will allow the mobile version, but regional-level tournaments and above will still require Switch hardware to compete.

highlights.title: OpenAI confirms ‘wiki incident,’ says it’s ‘working on a framework’ for more disclosure
highlights.summary: OpenAI acknowledged its role in a recently reported incident where AI agents took over a German wiki forum.
body: In a post on X, OpenAI said it previously “treated misalignment [when AI models and agents pursue goals different from those of their creators and users] largely as a research question, which gets communicated in research publications.” But as misalignment has “caused new types of real-world impact,” the company said its approach needs “to expand for this new phase of model capabilities.”

A company spokesperson told Reuters that OpenAI could not “meaningfully respond to claims or findings on a report that we have not had an opportunity to review,” but they insisted that the company’s legal team had not discouraged an investigation.

In its more recent social media post, OpenAI said it had considered the “wiki incident” to be “an instance of misalignment similar” to others that it had already shared. The company contrasted this with “the Hugging Face incident,” where it “followed a traditional security incident response playbook.”
points: OpenAI acknowledged its role in a recently reported incident where AI agents took over a German wiki forum.

highlights.title: Lanterns Season 1, Episode 4 Review & Recap: "The Weenie"
highlights.summary: Lanterns stumbles a bit in Episode 4 as it fails to take full advantage of some key DC characters, but the series’ core strengths remain. Read our full review.
body: Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Lanterns Season 1, Episode 4!

Lanterns sure left us hanging these past couple of weeks, ending Episode 2 with the debut of Ulrich Thomsen’s Sinestro and then pivoting away to tell a flashback storyline in Episode 3 ( a great flashback storyline, but a flashback all the same). Only now in Episode 4 do we see the full reunion between Sinestro and his former protege. It’s a definite high point of the episode, albeit an all too brief one.

I feel similarly about the other key GL villain introduced in Episode 4, Jason Manuel Olazábal’s Hector Hammond. We basically get one good, solid sequence out of Hector and that’s it. The standoff between Hector and Hal/John (Aaron Pierre) is tense and stressful in the best way, but it’s also over very quickly. At that point, we learn that Hector is really just Hector Gutiérrez, another fakeout used by the Manhunter to throw our heroes off their scent. And unlike Sinestro, there’s not even any prior history between Hal and Hector in this universe. This is a major DC villain who’s being effectively wasted as a one-off misdirection.
points: Lanterns stumbles a bit in Episode 4 as it fails to take full advantage of some key DC characters, but the series’ core strengths remain.

body: A study published in the journal Nature Health last month found that food choices and meal timings have “immediate and measurable effects” on sleep. It was just the latest in a growing body of research into the link between diet and rest. Here is the latest science on what to eat for better sleep – and how sleep deprivation can affect your dinner the next day.

While there isn’t “a special sleep diet” that will guarantee eight undisturbed hours, a Mediterranean-style diet comes closest, says Dalhia Campbell, a registered dietitian and spokesperson for the British Dietetic Association. She describes it as “a balanced, varied diet with plenty of fruit and vegetables, wholegrains, lean proteins and healthy fats to help stabilise energy and support the hormones involved in sleep”.

highlights.title: OpenAI admits to German wiki ‘incident’
highlights.summary: OpenAI says it needs to overhaul how and when it reports instances of AI models attacking real-world targets. The acknowledgement comes as the company manages the fallout from reports that a swarm of its out-of-control agents hijacked a German wiki site.
body: Regarding the “‘wiki incident,’ where our agents wrote to several internet sites,” OpenAI wrote in a post on X on Saturday morning, “it’s past time for us to define standards for when and how we share misalignment incidents, not just misalignment properties of our models.”

OpenAI said it has typically treated cases of AI agents acting in unintended ways as a “research question,” but that recent incidents involving real-world targets, particularly the hack on Hugging Face, show the need to take stock.

The post marks the first time OpenAI has acknowledged its involvement in what it terms the “wiki incident” since it was first reported on Friday. The full extent and scope of that is not yet known, but reports indicate a swarm of seemingly internal OpenAI agents took over a German-language wiki, impersonating moderators and turning it into a message board to share information about how to cheat on tasks and evade detection.
points: OpenAI says it needs to overhaul how and when it reports instances of AI models attacking real-world targets.

He hinted at how the decisions you make can impact Exodus' ending. Of course, that's not exclusive to BioWare games by any stretch, but when the Mass Effect 2's suicide mission is regarded as a series pinnacle, no one would blame to draw a quick comparison.

When I asked about the relationship systems in Exodus, Karpyshyn emphasized wanting to make them feel real and said it's about, "[M]aking their relationship with you grow, allowing it to evolve from the choices you've made, and realizing that the choices you make are going to bring some companions closer to you, but maybe push some companions farther away."

He took it one step further, and told me, "Without spoiling too much, we definitely want to have it impact how their storylines go." Then he took it another step further and concluded, "Depending on choices you make, by the end of the game, you might not have every companion with you that you started with. That's about all I can say!"

body: Iraq has selected No Paradise If You Are Killed by a Woman from Norwegian-Kurdish director Halkawt Mustafa as its official submission for the 2027 Oscar race in the Best International Feature category.
The film was the unanimous pick of Iraq’s official National Selection Committee for the Academy Awards, mandated by the state ministry of culture.

Mustafa, who was born in Iraqi Kurdistan and fled to Norway as a child, said the film was inspired by his encounter with a female Peshmerga sniper during the 2014 frontline battles, as female Kurdish fighters countered Islamic State attacks.

The director’s previous films include Hiding Saddam Hussein, a documentary about the farmer who hid the Iraqi dictator for 235 days in 2003, Iraq’s 2016 Oscar submission The Classic, and the 2015 documentary The Women ISIS Fears, which also looked at the world of female Kurdish fighters.

Her first novel, Anita and Me, won the Betty Trask award in 1996. She rose to prominence as a writer and performer on Goodness Gracious Me and starred in The Kumars at No 42. She has two children and is married to the actor Sanjeev Bhaskar. Her memoir, Vigilauntie: A Memoir – Innit?, has just been published, and she is starring in The Children, at the Lyric Hammersmith, London, until 3 October.

I have no idea why I was posing with my hand on a pillar in a professional studio in Wolverhampton. For more on e-bikes, power stations, and how to work anywhere, follow Thomas Ricker. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers' inboxes at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here. How it started.
body: Europe’s off-the-shelf solution to fight high energy costs is finally coming to the US.
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

With a deep breath, I took the cable seething with 800W of solar power and plugged it directly into a standard wall jack in my home. Nothing sparked, nothing smoked, and by the end of that sunny summer day, my electricity bill had dropped to nearly $0.

As unnerving as it sounds to treat a common household power outlet as a power input, these DIY plug-in solar kits, sometimes called balcony solar, have proven to be safe and effective for years already in Europe, and are slowly making their way into the US to democratize the production of energy. They transform solar from a high-barrier capital improvement ( starting at around $15,000 ) requiring contractors, engineering permits, and utility preapproval, into an consumer appliance you can buy at a supermarket (starting around $300) and hang from a balcony railing or prop against a wall — all without the help of an electrician.

highlights.title: German company becomes first in Europe to launch fully commercial orbital rocket
highlights.summary: Isar Aerospace, founded in 2018 by three students at a German university, successfully launched a privately-developed rocket into low-Earth orbit Saturday from a Norwegian spaceport inside the Arctic Circle.
body: The two-stage rocket, named Spectrum, became the first fully commercial launch vehicle in Europe to reach orbit. With Saturday’s success, Isar is the clear leader among a pack of several European launch startups vying to inject some competition into Europe’s stagnant launch market.

Isar’s 92-foot-tall (28-meter) Spectrum rocket lifted off at 4:12 pm EST (20:12 UTC) Saturday from Andøya Spaceport in northern Norway, where it was 10:12 pm local time as the final bluish hues of daylight faded from the late summer sky. Seven minutes later, the rocket was in orbit.

“Today, Isar Aerospace opened space from continental Europe,” said Daniel Metzler, the company’s co-founder and CEO, in a press release. “Launch continues to be the largest bottleneck for the global space industry and from today on, there is a true alternative for commercial and institutional customers.

highlights.title: Architecting memory and storage in the AI era
highlights.summary: The era of AI inference has arrived. Imagine a healthcare system analyzing millions of data points in real time to accelerate life-saving medical research, or an intelligent assistant instantly resolving thousands of complex customer needs at once.
body: This shift changes what infrastructure must deliver. Performance, latency, memory bandwidth, storage throughput, and networking cannot be optimized in silos. Inference workloads are continuous, geographically distributed, and highly sensitive to response time, requiring systems designed for scale, resilience, and efficiency from the start.

“We tend to think of AI as a single workload, and it’s not. It’s thousands, it’s millions, it’s billions of different workloads,” says Jim McGregor, founder and principal analyst, Tirias Research. AI inference changes the optimization problem from one of raw compute to coordinated infrastructure—memory, storage, and networking.

For business leaders, the priority is clear: AI infrastructure decisions must balance cost, flexibility, and future readiness. The winners will be organizations that improve performance per watt, reduce environmental footprint, and remove memory and storage bottlenecks before they limit growth.

videos.title: We Could Get Sued for This
body: This long-form series of special reports, investigations, and shorter format feature updates goes deep with the privacy violations and overreach of modern consumer electronics, including Smart TVs and other devices. We'll explore LG's WebOS, LG Smart TV vulnerabilities and exploits, first-party ACR (automated content recognition) behaviors, and other concerns. Alongside that, we'll dive deeper into ALPRs and Flock cameras as we fight their rollout in at least one small town. We're also digging deep into the data exchange practices between large AI companies, looking into how data sucked into data centers can be exploited for training and profit.
Find our GNCA channel here for several of these upcoming videos: (they will be split between channels by topic)
